profile.headline: Software Engineer
profile.summary:
Currently a Senior Software Engineer.

Graduated from Queen’s University Belfast with First Class Honours in a Masters of Engineering in Computer Science.

positions.title: Software Designer
positions.description:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise's Big Data division.

Developed massively scalable, resilient, distributed data-processing microservices using Docker, Apache Mesos, Marathon and queue-based messaging services such as RabbitMQ and Apache Kafka. 

Examples of applications I am actively involved in:
- https://github.com/WorkerFramework/worker-framework
- The microservice orchestration layer controlling the flow of job processing.
- RESTful web services using JAX-RS and Jersey.
- Java libraries wrapping C++ and python sources.

positions.title: Demonstrator
positions.description: Learned valuable teaching skills providing my own experience and knowledge to support first year and second year students in Java Programming and Reasoning for Problem Solving module practicals and projects.

positions.title: Student Intern
Software Engineering Intern
positions.description:
• Built Java Enterprise web applications using Java 1.6.
• MVC pattern using Javascript controllers.
• Created and maintained database stored procedures and DBUnit tests. 
• Participated in test driven development, created JUnit tests, FitNesse automated acceptance tests.
• Worked with SAP HANA, SAPUI5, iOS.

honors.title: Degree Plus Award
honors.description:
Degree Plus was introduced in October 2008 to provide Queen's students with a vehicle for accrediting learning and skills developed through extracurricular activities and programs.

This award recognises contributions during the Project Children internship program, where the student has shown they have learned valuable employability skills from their participation.
honors.issuer: Issued by Queen's University Belfast · May 2015

honors.title: Queen's Employability and Skills Award
honors.description:
The Queen’s Employability and Skills Award is an innovative programme which enables students to gain an accredited award which recognises skills developed through different types of casual work, short term placement, volunteering or involvement in clubs and societies.Significant numbers of students do not have formal work placement opportunity within their degree programme, however, may aquire a wide range of employability skills by engaging in other work related activities.  The programme delivered by the careers service enables participants to gain a theoretical and practical understanding of the skills they are developing.  It also involves training on how to reflect on the experience and make the link between work experience, transferable skills and graduate employments.

This award recognises contributions during the Project Children internship program, where the student has shown they have learned valuable employability skills from their participation.
honors.issuer: Issued by Queen's University Belfast · May 2015
